column2: An incredibly thick jungle, completely infested with spiders. Infested jungles such as these sometimes start expanding in a planet's biosphere, if the conditions are right. These worlds usually have to be bombarded from orbit with atomic weapons, to avoid the spiders being unwittingly (or worse, on purpose) transported to other inhabited planets.\n\n<color=#d73b33>Biome difficulty: Very hard. This is a VERY hostile biome. Don't start your base here unless you know very well what you are doing. Build a walled compound, leave it as seldom as possible, and USE the spiders in your advantage.</color>

This desertic landscape appears to be perpetually covered in an unnatural fog that seeps all light from the sun. In the ancient past it was partly terraformed by a mysterious humanoid alien race simply known as Forsakens. A plethora of nocturnal alien creatures roam the desert, feeding on bioluminescent plants and fungi that are the only available and reliable source of light.

<color=#AE6233>Biome difficulty: Hard. Luminosity in this biome doesn't reach high enough levels to grow plants, so you'll have to use the flora as natural sunlamps, and all ranged weapons will get a huge penalty. Nights are DARK, and most creatures are nocturnal. Those which aren't, won't last long.</color>

NOTE: The latest changes made by Ludeon to the glow grid make this biome much more performant than it was! Enjoy!.

These parched mudflats are littered with the ancient bones of colossal Gallatrosses. Apparently the highly intelligent beasts are coming here to die, and to mourn their fallen relatives.\n\n<color=#7C9233>Biome difficulty: Intermediate. Mostly equal to an Arid Shrubland. Don't mess with the Gallatross unless you are very sure you are prepared, though.</color>

A huge mold-like organism has grown in this area, basically destroying the previous existing ecosystem, and replacing it with an alien landscape of its own creation. Its strange biology seems to be compatible with this planet's biosphere.\n\n<color=#5CB033>Biome difficulty: Easy. Expect to find no useable rocky materials to build here, and very little wood, but plenty of food.</color>

Product of ancient terraforming, these open grasslands were designed to be an utopian paradise: giant flowers provide both construction materials and sustenance, while an abundance of wildlife creates ample ranching and hunting possibilities. There are no extremes in these pristine fields, making them ideal for long term habitation.\n\n<color=#33d733>Biome difficulty: Very easy. This biome is intended to be an even easier version of the temperate forest. Mild temperatures, very few predators, abundance of resources and lack of serious diseases.</color>

A mechanoid hive was dismantling this biome, turning its mass into computronium, and hastily left it abandoned for unknown reasons. Almost no trace of its biological origins has been left untouched, with even the trees turned into mechanical contraptions destined for some nefarious purposes.\n\n<color=#7C9233>Biome difficulty: Intermediate. Animals rarely come to this biome, and thus finding food can be VERY difficult. Soil fertility is atrocious. Metals are incredibly common.</color>

Mangrove swamps, also known as mangals, are coastal wetlands found in tropical and subtropical regions. They are characterized by halophytic (salt loving) trees, shrubs and other plants growing in brackish to saline tidal waters. This mangrove swamp is plagued by parasites, tropical diseases and bio-engineered viruses, making it an inhospitable place.\n\n<color=#AE6233>Biome difficulty: Hard, harder than a tropical swamp. Diseases will strike very often, including some exotic ones that will test your skill.</color>

The Mycotic Jungle is a super dense overgrowth of massive giant mushrooms, covered in a coat of mycelium. Giant mushrooms can be used as a poor substitute for wood, and the smaller ones will provide some sustenance. Beware of the bigger mushrooms, though, as they create a cloud of dangerous spores that can quickly suffocate any organic life.\n\n<color=#5CB033>Biome difficulty: Easy. Rains are VERY common in this biome. There is a plant that produces renewable wood, but most of the flora produces mushroom stalks.</color>

This sickly looking forest seems to be completely alien, probably of an extra-dimensional origin. Natural plant life seems to be struggling to grow, and the very ground fights against the neighbouring lands. Strange lifeforms, perhaps not entirely alive, scurry around the sickening vegetation.\n\n<color=#7C9233>Biome difficulty: Intermediate. A strange red fog reduces ranged accuracy almost constantly and reduces colonists' mood. There is a plant that produces renewable wood, but most of the flora produces red wood, a poor substitute.</color>

Huge liquid propane lakes fill this desolate frozen landscape. As propane is a compound that doesn't occur naturally, this is probably the remnant of some weird ecological or industrial experiment gone awry.\n\n<color=#AE6233>Biome difficulty: Hard, but not as hard as Sea Ice. Expect extremely cold temperatures, constant snowing, very little and non-renewable wood, and usually no rocks. Surprisingly, some strange flora have adapted to these circumstances, attracting all kinds of unusual animals.</color>

A desolate expanse of obsidian and solidified lava, with several active calderas bubbling menacingly. A few scraggy trees cling to the mostly unfertile soil.\n\n<color=#d73b33>Biome difficulty: Very hard. A permanent heat wave will raise temperature permanently by 30ºC. Acid rain will fall every few quadrums, which might be a welcome respite from the constant volcanic ash, if it weren't burning your colonists with acid. Ravenous exotic animals will set your stuff on fire. Fire, fire everywhere. You have been warned!</color>

Sun-baked mud, interspersed with patches of fertile grassy terrain. And, of course, the tar lakes themselves. Tar pits are usually infested with extensive subterranean bumbledrone hives.\n\n<color=#5CB033>Biome difficulty: Easy. This biome is arid, but rich in animal and vegetal life. Wood is not a problem, and neither are foreageable plants. Stone is scarce due to the pits being always a flat terrain. The greatest hazard is the incredibly hard to cross terrain, specially around the pits. Also, beware of aggressive bumbledrones surrounding their hive entrances!</color>

Toxic gas emissions from nearby volcanically active calderas are precipitating in the form of dangerous acid rain. Acid rain has an adverse impact on flora and fauna, killing insect and aquatic life-forms as well as having impacts on human health.

The extreme heat produced by the magma lakes bakes this region. Large plumes of superheated air rise from the lava, heating their surroundings and making them barely inhabitable.

The superorganism retains echoes of past events, stored like data in a living neural lattice. These memory echoes occasionally (every 2 days) bleed into reality, causing inspirations, mood boosts, penalties... or hallucinations.
Low levels of background radiation permeate the area, subtly affecting health and mutation rates, and causing gene mutations in random colonists every quadrum or so.
Wild swings between scorching days and freezing nights challenge survival and crop stability.
Something in this area makes all animals explode violently on death.
The ubiquitous presence of fungal spores makes staying outdoors almost unbearable.
Active psychotropic fungus in the bloodstream. They improve consciousness and decrease the need to rest.
A built-up tolerance to psychotropic fungus. The more severe this tolerance is, the more psychotropic fungus it takes to get the same effect.

A chemical addiction to psychotropic fungus. Long-term use of psychotropic fungus has caused neurological adaptations at the cellular level, so the brain can no longer function properly without the drug.\n\nWithout regular doses of psychotropic fungus, withdrawal symptoms will begin. However, extended abstinence will force the brain to adapt back to its normal state, resolving the addiction.

Raw rime nodules are filled with a naturally processed propane compound that is mildy euphoric for humans, similar to ethanol. Chemically speaking, this is unlikely, hinting at a non-natural origin for these strange flora.

This person has developed a very strong allergy to airborne spores and / or plant pollen. This allergy will make breathing difficult, but it will go away (for now) if treated properly.
This animal has developed a strong allergy to airborne spores and / or plant pollen. This allergy will make breathing difficult, but it will go away (for now) if treated properly.
A fast acting toxin is coursing through this creature's veins, paralyzing his muscles. It will wear off after a while.
A ravaging genetically engineered tapeworm has infected this person.\n\n<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> Will increase severity unless treated. It will go away after a total tend quality of 3.

Most likely artificially created as a bio-weapon, this perverse virus attacks the victim's motor cortex eventually leaving the person immobilized.\n\n<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> Treatable, immunizable disease.

A fast-growing bacterial disease that causes gangrene, with skin progressively blackening and falling off. If treated properly, it will be cured in 3-4 days. Even if treated, the colonist may lose a toe or finger or two.
Death of body tissue due to a lack of blood flow or a serious bacterial infection.
Slime in your eyes blinds you for a while. Also, yuck.
Nodules of chemfuel will cause this creature to blow up when killed.
An installed animal eldritch flesh tentacle. A fleshy, muscled tentacle resembling a partial transformation into a fleshbeast.

A malevolent looking, bloodshot eye is emerging from this wound, blinking and peering wildly around it. Without treatment, it will cause rotting of the local tissue, eventually causing blood poisoning and death. They will however allow the afflicted to see through them.
Moving through quicksand. Greatly reduces movement speed.
The colonist is subconsciously affected by the mechanoid resonance receiver’s low-frequency harmonics. Stress signals in the brain are dampened, enhancing focus and emotional stability.

Cookie sand in the eyes. It impairs vision, but can be cleared within a few moments.

A red wod floor crafted with the exotic wood found in an ocular forest.
A pseudo-wooden floor using the material from crystalline trees as planks.
A hard surface made of asphalt.
Painstaikingly pulverizing mudstone and mixing it with water allows colonists to turn the fine sand into a compacted sand surface, capable of holding some constructions.
A dense mat of organic flesh that clings loosely to the ground.

A flat wooden surface on supportive beams which can be built over water. You can build light structures on bridges, but be careful - bridges are fragile. If a bridge falls, buildings on top of it fall as well.
These fungi taste funny and produce a potent mood-increasing chemical high. However, if eaten too often, they can generate a mild addiction.
The sacs of a very strange plant, partly inorganic, that seems to extract propane from the surrounding landscape and store it as an energy source. These sacs can be consumed as a very mild euphoric.
A massive duct that drops endlessly into the ground. It will regularly vent freezing cold air from an underground megastructure, dramatically lowering the temperature of the surrounding area.
A massive duct that drops endlessly into the ground. It will regularly vent large amounts of sickly looking smoke that will plunge the area into a preternatural darkness.
A massive duct that drops endlessly into the ground. It will regularly vent huge red clouds of a vaporized blood-like substance that will coalesce into a disgusting blood rain.
A massive duct that drops endlessly into the ground. It will regularly vent clouds of microscopic self-powered archites that affect corpses reanimating them to create a twisted imitation of life.
A moderately-sized archotech tower rising from the ground. It seems to be long inert.
A large archotech structure. The dull green surface is ruiend and covered in vegetation. It seems to be long inert.
The ruined central core of an archonexus. Its broad surfaces are dusty and covered with vegetation. It seems to be long inert.
A ruined mech turret base. Completely broken.
A ruined mech turret. Completely broken. No useful components can be scavenged from this old turret.
A spent mech shield generator. Still faintly humming.
A ruined mech auto-mortar. Completely broken. No useful components can be scavenged from this old mortar.
A ruined mech large turret base. Whatever this base held, it's long gone.
A ruined mech power cell. Perhaps a few components can be scavenged from this one.
A ruined mech proximity activator. Perhaps a few components can be scavenged from this one.
A ruined mech capsule. Thankfully it has been empty for a while.
A ruined mech assembler. Thankfully it has been inactive for a while.
This was once a relaxing swimming pool, but it is now a fetid, stagnant pool of water.
A recliner used for relaxation. Rotten and dirty to the point of uselessness.
A beach umbrella so broken that it won't even keep the sun out.
A half-deflated beach ball that has seen better days.
This pool ladder has seen better days.
A deflated and dirty pool float.

A containment vat designed to preserve and regulate the life of a Gamma plant beyond its natural span. Suspended in nutrient gel and restrained by growth-limiting harnesses, the plant glows with its characteristic brilliance, enough to replace a sun lamp, while its metabolic decay is slowed to a crawl.\n\nRadagast berries are needed to build it to create the nutrient gel that sustains the plant.
This ribcage once belonged to a living Gallatross of truly exceptional size. Can be deconstructed to acquire ancient bones.
This skull belonged to an exceptionally huge Gallatross. Look at the size of this thing! Can be deconstructed to acquire ancient bones.
This fosilized bone might have belonged to an exceptionally large Gallatross. Can be deconstructed to acquire ancient bones.
This fosilized bone might have belonged to an exceptionally large Gallatross. Can be deconstructed to acquire ancient bones.
These fosilized bones might have belonged to an exceptionally large Gallatross. Can be deconstructed to acquire ancient bones.
These fosilized bones might have belonged to an exceptionally large Gallatross. Can be deconstructed to acquire ancient bones.
A powerful hydraulic drill designed to bore into ancient bone deposits buried deep beneath the ground, breaking them loose for extraction and processing.
A bulky, churning machine that grinds down organic slime and compresses it under immense pressure, slowly transforming the ooze into dense, usable sandstone.
A mysterious crashed piece of a spaceship. This was probably full of mechanoids once, but it seems to have been left abandoned for a while. Perhaps it could be salvaged for raw materials.

A wide band receiver designed to intercept lingering mechanoid signal patterns from the environment. It decodes the residual overclocking hum into a low-frequency auditory resonance: barely perceptible, yet strangely calming.
A chunk of sugar. It can be deconstructed to acquire some sugar (if you are using VE Cooking).
A sandstone pillar warped into an unnatural form.
A large spire made of solid obsidian.
A specialized synthetizer that extracts neutroamine from the cerebrospinal fluid of vast surface lakes, processing it into a usable form.
Collects edible airborne micro-fungi present in this map and extracts them into processed fungi that can be used as a food ingredient.
Uses alcyonite solar cells to extract electricity from the sun. Produces extra electricity if a red fog weather is present. Does not work in the dark or under artificial light.
Uses alcyonite solar cells to extract electricity from the sun. Produces extra electricity if a red fog weather is present. Does not work in the dark or under artificial light.
This device needs a small amount of electricity to condense atmospheric gases and spew a large cloud of ocular gas. This gas blocks ranged attacks greatly, working as a constant smokepop belt.
An experimental device that emmanates strange waves making everyone love the truly alien weather.
The core sample drill allows you to acquire standard rock types not usually present in a particular biome. It needs to drill pretty deep to do so, and thus it costs quite a lot to build.
A propane-fueled stove with an attached countertop for preparing meals.
A propane-fueled station for smithing non-mechanical weapons and tools.
Extracts usable metal from slag chunks and other mixed metal items.
A work station for assembling machinery like guns and ammunition, or breaking down dead mechanoids.

A device that burns propane fuel and turns it into heat. The propane heater wastes a lot of fuel when attempting to reach temperatures too different from ambient ones, but it's quite fuel conservative if configured carefully.
A portable flamethrower turret fueled with propane. May explode when damaged. Its dumb AI brain can't be directly controlled, so beware of friendly fire.
A propane flamethrower made to be mounted on a turret.
A fiery fissure in the earth that intermittently erupts with jets of molten rock and searing gas.
Produces electricity from hyperheated geothermal steam geysers in a magma rich zone. Must be placed on a steam geyser.

A door built using exotic materials. Simple doors must be manually opened, which slows people down. The amount of slowdown depends on what the door is made of, though exotic doors open and close slightly faster than regular counterparts, at the cost of increased building costs.
An autodoor built using exotic materials. Powered operation allows people to move through the door without slowing down. Requires more materials than normal autodoors but also less power to work.
An impassable wall built using exotic materials. Slightly stronger than regular walls.
An impassable block made of fosilized, solid bone. Whatever creature this bone belonged to is long gone.
A column built using exotic materials. Does not block sight or movement and looks quite nice.
An impassable wall. Capable of holding up a roof.
Chunks of smoothed compacted chocolate. Is this revolting? Well, yes, yes it is.
Extracts tar from a natural tar hole and transforms the tar into chemfuel.

A pair of tar shells connected to a trigger which detonates on touch or bullet impact. Since it is hidden in the surrounding terrain, it cannot be placed adjacent to other traps. Animals can sense these when calm. Creates a puddle of tar that is very difficult to move across. It is also very difficult to remove, and tends to also remove other floors because it sticks to them and ruins them. All things considered, I wouldn't detonate one of this in my kitchen.
A natural hole in the mud connecting to an underground tar reservoir. This will periodically spray fresh tar in the vicinity.

A huge mound of hardened organic matter that communicates with an extensive underground hive. Bumbledrones will periodically exit this hive to gather food for the bumbledrone colony. Bumbledrones surrounding a hive are particularly aggressive, so it's best to give them some space.
These hardened chunks of slime can be used as a last chance alternative to starvation. Barely edible, and absolutely disgusting.
Raw fungus. This variety lasts a longer time without rotting, making it more valuable.
Even though these mushrooms look weird, they are very nice to eat, even when raw.
Raw fungus. These particular fungi are more nutritive than usual, but there is a greater chance for them to cause food poisoning.
Raw slime. This thing is edible. Barely.
Raw Crystal Horn. Only partially organic: part of its structure is clearly crystalline. Edible, but uncomfortably crunchy.
These translucent plants seem to be able to grow almost anywhere, even in some snow covered areas. They can be dried in a fire and used to feed herbivore animals efficiently.
The blue nodules grow at the end of each branch / tentacle of a tentacular plant, and they produce an eerie rattling sound from time to time.
The fleshy bright red fruit of an iashiphus plant.
The water-filled bulbs of a brown barrel cactus. Quite tasteless.
These soft bulbs are exceptionally sweet, an ideal condiment for any dish.

These fruit seem to be as hard as the trunk of the plant they are harvested from, and equally covered in spines. The inner flesh of the fruit tastes like blood-drenched meat, and herbivore animals will refuse to consume it.

This blob of organic matter is produced by bumbledrone caretakers, a caste of bumbledrones that never leaves the subterranean part of the hives. It provides sustenance for bumbledrones who need to leave the hive for any reason, such as foraging or hunting.
The seeds of the sunflower plant are more commonly eaten as a snack than as part of a meal. They can also be used as garnishes or ingredients in various recipes. These seeds are gigantic!
Alcyonite is a very rare variation of the almandite gemstone. Really strong, able to easily cut steel, yet malleable and with interesting piezoelectric capabilities.

These brittle crystalline strands can be extracted from crystal flowers. Not flammable, but not strong at all. Internally, the are formed by a fine lattice of exotic crystals, creating a structure that is incredibly good at maintaining a constant temperature.
This red tinged wood is oddly strong, and a sweet scent emanates from it. Less flammable than terrestrial wood, but quite ugly.
These mushroom stalks have been hardened by age until they are almost as firm as a low quality wood. Very flammable, and not very resistant.

Dried chunks of cordax resin. A viscous slurry of organic compounds, this nectar-like liquid is used by the carnivorous Keening Cordax plant to trap insects. It is extremely sticky and can be used as a very efficient sealant.

Asphalt, or bitumen, is a sticky, black and highly viscous liquid or semi-solid, composed almost entirely of petroleum. It is present in most crude petroleums and in some natural deposits, such as tar pits.\n\nAsphalt can be used to build tarmac roads, greatly increasing movement in difficult terrains.

A versatile fuel. Can be converted into chemfuel, or used as fuel for propane specific buildings, such as heaters or stoves. Insert inane and trite King of the Hill joke here (yes, I have heard them all, you are not original).
A sturdy building material made from the remains of long-dead creatures. Though aged and brittle, it can be worked much like wood into structures and furnishings.

A huge bioluminescent globular plant. Can be used as a natural darklight sunlamp to grow regular plants, though the toxic environment it grows at might not be the best for cultivation. Note that light-sensitive plants such as domesticated Stikehr and mushrooms should be kept far away from them.

Plant details: Toxic Gamma is a wild plant. It needs no light, and produces 100% darklight on its own, which is enough to grow other plants around it.

Based on artwork by Yevheniia Rodina, https://dribbble.com/Rodina

A giant alien mushroom that glows in the strange darkening mist. This stikehr has adapted to a very polluted environment, and produces a meager amount of wood. \n\nPlant details: Polluted Stikehr is a wild plant that can only grow in polluted terrains. It needs no light, and produces 50% darklight on its own, not enough to grow other plants around it. Can be harvested for normal wood.
One of the weirdest plants from Earth, genetically modified to thrive in wet, warm environments.
An unusually tall plant with bright, pink nodules. Its nodules are slightly toxic for humans, and it produces a strange, rotten fruit smell, so it is considered absolutely inedible.

A rare, huge flower which can be found in the deepest jungles. Its quite striking colour and nice smell makes it popular in gardening, if it can be extracted from the deep jungle, of course.\n\nBased on artwork by Rob Smyth, https://robsmythart.com/projects
A towering, ancient tree with dense foliage and thick, twisting roots—its canopy forms part of the near-impenetrable roof of the deep jungle.\n\nBased on concept art for plants for Guild Wars.

This jungle polux tree has adapted so perfectly to polluted soil and airborne toxins that it doesn't even need to remove pollution from its environment.

Plant details: Deep jungle polux trees are a wild plant, and they need minimum terrain fertility of 0.05. Can only grow in polluted terrains. Can be harvested for small amounts of Red Wood. Tree lover ideologies don't much care about chopping down these weird trees.

Based on art by Corndoggy and Motones, https://www.deviantart.com/motones/art/Xeno-Plants-503932885

A short toxin-adapted shrub with berries so unbelievably toxic that no animal would ever dare consume them.

Plant details:Difficult to move through, it slows down anyone moving over it. It can only grow in polluted areas.

Based on artwork by Rob Smyth, https://robsmythart.com/projects

A giant alien mushroom that glows in the strange darkening mist. Contrary to the smaller domesticated strands, the giant Stikehr can grow in light environments, as long as it is protected by the Forsaken mists. Its stalk is so hardened that it can be considered wood for all intents and purposes. 

Plant details: Giant Stikehr is a cultivated plant that also appears in the wild, and it needs minimum terrain fertility of 0.7. It needs no light, and produces 50% light on its own, not enough to grow other plants around it. Can be harvested for normal wood.

Based on art by Tyson Roberts, https://www.artstation.com/tyson

This Septimum plant has grown to an enormous size, with a flowering top as large as a person. Domesticated septimum plants are used as a source of Ultima fibers, but this exemplar is way too old and its fibers are too hard to be used in a practical way.\n\nPlant details: Giant Septimum is a wild plant that cannot be cultivated, and it needs minimum terrain fertility of 0.7. It needs no light.
Wild grass. Grows anywhere there is a little light and minimally fertile ground.

This twisting alien plant grows small glowing berries that can be harvested and consumed. Radagast berries can be used as a base for a growth medium to stabilize gamma plants.\n\nPlant details: Wild Ragadast is a wild plant that cannot be cultivated, and it needs minimum terrain fertility of 0.7. It needs no light, and produces 50% light on its own, not enough to grow other plants around it.

Like many other flora from the Forsakens native planet, this huge globular plant is bioluminescent. Smaller specimens can be used as a decorative light source, whereas this wild exemplar emits so much light that it can be used as a natural sunlamp to grow regular plants. Note that light-sensitive plants such as domesticated Stikehr and mushrooms should be kept far away from them.

Plant details: Giant Gamma is a cultivated plant that also appears in the wild, and it needs minimum terrain fertility of 0.7. It needs no light, and produces 100% light on its own, which is enough to grow other plants around it.

Inspired by an iStockPhoto collection: https://www.istockphoto.com/en/vector/beautiful-fantasy-mushrooms-set-gm665380048-121272853

This strange plant seems to be of alien origins. It doesn't seem to be fit for human consumption. Its common name alludes to the tea-bag shape of its flowers, and the fact that its sap is a very sticky substance.\n\nInspired by art by Desiree-m. Deviantart page no longer exists :(
A plant of the euphorbia genus, commonly called spurges. This plant has adapted to arid climates and stores a lot of water inside their spine-covered leaves.

Despite its common name, the dead bower tree is not truly dead, just exceptionally adapted to survival in arid weather. The tree produces huge leaves every few decades. These leaves harness energy via photosynthesis, and this chemical energy is stored in brown coloured chemical postules that act as natural batteries. The tree then uses that energy slowly over the following years, only producing more leaves when it is depleted.
Although at first sight this seems to be an independent plant, its roots are intricately interconnected with the rest of the gelatinous superorganism.
Although at first sight this seems to be an independent plant, its roots are intricately interconnected with the rest of the gelatinous superorganism.
Wild tall grass. Slows down anyone moving over it.
This tree doesn't seem to be entirely solid. Upon further examination, it isn't an independent entity, its roots fusing seamlessly with the hardened gelatinous ground.
This tree doesn't seem to be entirely solid. Upon further examination, it isn't an independent entity, its roots fusing seamlessly with the hardened gelatinous ground.
This slimy bulb seems to be feeding on the polluted terrain like a parasite.
A plant of the euphorbia genus, commonly called spurges. This plant is a variety of the Euphorbia Rimworldia plant that has adapted to polluted environments.

Lithops is a genus of succulent plants often known as pebble plants or living stones, due to their stone-like appearance that allows them to avoid being eaten by blending in with surrounding rocks. This gigantic lithops has been genetically modified to actually gather small amounts of metals and stone and incorporate them into its structure. Who said geneticists lack a sense of humour?\n\nPlant details: Gargantuan lithops is a wild plant that cannot be cultivated, and it needs minimum terrain fertility of 0.7. Can be harvested for steel and a stone chunk.

Giant flowers genetically modified by a long-forgotten genetics company using the genome of a hibiscus plant. These seem to be blooming almost continuously. Their stalks are not strong enough to be used as a wood substitute, but they are incredibly pretty.

Plant details: Giant mutant hibiscus is a wild plant that cannot be cultivated. Very beautiful.

Based on a tileset from Kokoro Reflections: https://kokororeflections.com/product/kr-flower-forest-tileset-for-rpgs/

Giant flowers genetically modified by a long-forgotten genetics company using the genome of the common sunflower plant. These seem to be blooming almost continuously. Their stalks are very strong and durable, so they can be cut and used as a wood substitute, while the flower itself also produces sunflower seeds that can be consumed by both animals and colonists.

Plant details: Giant sunflower is a cultivated plant that also appears in the wild, and it needs minimum terrain fertility of 0.7. Can be harvested for wood and giant sunflower seeds.

Based on a tileset from Kokoro Reflections: https://kokororeflections.com/product/kr-flower-forest-tileset-for-rpgs/

Giant flowers genetically modified by a long-forgotten genetics company using the genome of a tulip plant. These seem to be blooming almost continuously. Their stalks are very strong and durable, so they can be cut and used as a wood substitute.

Plant details: Giant tulip is a cultivated plant that also appears in the wild, and it needs minimum terrain fertility of 0.7. Can be harvested for wood.

Based on a tileset from Kokoro Reflections: https://kokororeflections.com/product/kr-flower-forest-tileset-for-rpgs/

A continously blooming giant flower with a dangerous, bright pink colour. Its stalk can be cut and used as a wood substitute.\n\nPlant details: Giant toxic flowers are wild plants that only grow in polluted ground. Can be harvested for meager amounts of wood.

This thing was once a tree. Mechanoids repurposed its cells into a half-tree, half-mechanoid abomination, serving an unknown purpose. Perhaps a bit of wood could be extracted from it.\n\nInspired by art by Desiree-m. Deviantart page no longer exists :(
Wild grass. Grows anywhere there is a little light and minimally fertile ground.

A tree that grows in saline or brackish water. They contain a complex salt filtration system and a complex root system to cope with saltwater immersion, and they are adapted to the low-oxygen conditions of waterlogged mud.\n\nPlant details: Mangrove trees are a cultivated plant that also appears in the wild, and it needs minimum terrain fertility of 1. Can be harvested for wood.

A weird, colourful plant adapted to extract nutrients from mangrove trees. Its own roots are covered in barbs capable of puncturing and integrating into the root systems of mangrove trees, acting as a parasitic organism. Its sap is slightly poisonous to many animals, but primates seem to be unaffected by it, and it can be used in fact as a crude herbal medicine.

Plant details: Parasitic mangrove is a wild plant that cannot be cultivated, and it needs minimum terrain fertility of 1. Can be harvested for herbal medicine.

Based on art by Tyson Roberts, https://www.artstation.com/tyson
A palm tree adapted to the mangrove conditions.\n\nBased on art by Tyson Roberts, https://www.artstation.com/tyson

A small brown mushroom typically found in caves. It smells like an old, dirty rag pulled from the stomach of a rotting muffalo - but it tastes surprisingly good when cooked. This glowstool variant has adapted to outside life, but produces very few edible caps when harvested.\n\nPlant details: Glowstool is a cultivated plant that also appears in the wild, and it needs minimum terrain fertility of 0.95. Can be harvested for raw fungus.

The lilac beacon is a tall mushroom with a bright purple cap. It is much more nutritive than other fungi, but it has a greater risk of being hard on the stomach. This variant has adapted to outside life, but produces very few edible caps when harvested.\n\nPlant details: Lilac beacon is a cultivated plant that also appears in the wild, and it needs minimum terrain fertility of 0.95. Can be harvested for purple raw fungus.

A small, ramified fungal colony with a pungent aroma. A witches' oyster produces caps that take quite a long time to deteriorate.

Plant details: Witches' Oyster is a cultivated plant that also appears in the wild, and it needs minimum terrain fertility of 0.95. Can be harvested for pink raw fungus.

Based on art by Alex Konstad, http://www.alexkonstad.com/

Everything about this fungus screams "I'm toxic, stay away from me". Of course this doesn't stop some enterprising individuals from consuming it as a drug. The agaricus domecap is a psychotropic fungus, and should be consumed with extreme precaution, if at all.

Plant details: Agaricus domecap is a cultivated plant that also appears in the wild, and it needs minimum terrain fertility of 0.95. Can be harvested for psychotropic fungus.

Based on art by Alex Konstad, http://www.alexkonstad.com/

An enormous purple mushroom. Its size and glowing protrusions make this fungus beautiful to look at. This agarilux variant has adapted to outside life, but produces very few edible caps when harvested.\n\nPlant details: Agarilux is a cultivated plant that also appears in the wild, and it needs minimum terrain fertility of 0.95. Can be harvested for purple raw fungus.

A colossal purple mushroom. Its size and glowing protrusions make this fungus beautiful to look at. Its stalk has been hardened, giving it a firmness similar to a weak wood.\n\nPlant details: Giant Agarilux is a cultivated plant that also appears in the wild, and it needs minimum terrain fertility of 0.95. Can be harvested for mushroom stalks.

A mycorrhiza is a symbiotic association between a fungus and a plant. This particular organism is highly advanced, and the two symbionts have almost fused into a single creature that keeps the supporting structures of the original tree (the trunk) and the caps and mycelium of the original fungus. A small quantity of wood can be harvested from its trunk.

Plant details: Arbuscular mycorrhiza is a cultivated plant that also appears in the wild, and it needs minimum terrain fertility of 0.95. Can be harvested for normal wood.

Based on art by Aphrodite: https://www.artstation.com/artwork/3ol4AB

A huge pink mushroom, constantly dribbling a pungent, resin-like substance. This substance is a potent neurotoxin that could potentially be extracted and used as a weapon.

Plant details: Dribbling cap is a cultivated plant that also appears in the wild, and it needs minimum terrain fertility of 0.95. Can be harvested for powerful single use poison darts.

Based on art by Alex Konstad, http://www.alexkonstad.com/

A big greyish mushroom. Its size and glowing protrusions make this fungus beautiful to look at. Its stalk has been hardened, giving it a firmness similar to a weak wood.

Plant details: Recurved stropharia is a cultivated plant that also appears in the wild, and it needs minimum terrain fertility of 0.95. Can be harvested for mushroom stalks.

Based on art by Alex Konstad, http://www.alexkonstad.com/

A blueish-pink mushroom, secreting a slimy substance that attracts insects. This substance paralyzes the insects, and eventually kills them, being used by the fungus as fertilizer. Strangely enough, the slimy substance gives this fungus a very rich taste, and it can even be consumed raw.

Plant details: Slimy pholiota is a cultivated plant that also appears in the wild, and it needs minimum terrain fertility of 0.95. Can be harvested for blue raw fungus.

Based on art by Alex Konstad, http://www.alexkonstad.com/

An enormous purple mushroom, glowing in darkness with a faint purple luminiscence. Its size and glowing protrusions make this fungus beautiful to look at. This agarilux variant has adapted to outside life, but produces very few edible caps when harvested.\n\nPlant details: Glowing agarilux is a wild plant that cannot be cultivated, and it needs minimum terrain fertility of 0.95. Can be harvested for raw purple fungus.
A blue moss typically found in deep, dark caves. It is sticky, with tangled fibers, which slows anyone walking over it. This bryolux variant has adapted to outside life.

An unbelievably large exemplar of Agarilux. This myconic colony has adapted perfectly to its environment, releasing large clouds of extremely dangerous spores that fill the air surrounding it. These spores attack both other fungi and roaming animals, and after they inevitably suffocate, the Agarilux Prime extends prehensile hyphae to feed on their rotting corpses.\n\nThe Agarilux Prime can be cut just like any other plant, but unless the person doing the cutting is perfectly protected against the toxic spores, it will probably prove to be a one-way mission. Or mortars... I guess mortars will work too.

A giant mushroom that has adapted to growing in extremely polluted environments.\n\nPlant details: Agaritox is a wild plant that can only grow in poilluted soil. Can be harvested for meager amounts of mushroom stalks.
A very strange purple coloured fungus that resembles a coral. Grows only in polluted soil.
This grass is very bizarre, probably not even 100% carbon based. Not very edible for terrestrial creatures.
This grass is very bizarre, probably not even 100% carbon based. Not very edible for terrestrial creatures.
This grass is very bizarre, probably not even 100% carbon based. Not very edible for terrestrial creatures.

This outlandish tree is not even 100% carbon based, and it seems to be struggling to grow from exposure to a terrestrial environment. Strange fruits resembling eyeballs hang from the tree, but they are probably not edible. Its wood releases a powerful, sweet scent. Perhaps it can be somehow useful.\n\nPlant details: Ocular Trees are a cultivated plant that also appears in the wild, and it needs minimum terrain fertility of 0.05. Can be harvested for Red Wood. Tree lover ideologies don't much care about chopping down these weird trees.

A strange infection seems to be transforming this regular oak into an ocular tree. It still retains its trunk and its leaves, though they are beginning to transform into pulsating red structures that don't seem to be able to survive in this universe. This tree might be useful to harvest a small amount of real wood.\n\nPlant details: Half transformed ocular trees are a wild plant that cannot be cultivated, and it needs minimum terrain fertility of 0.05. Can be harvested for normal wood.

An outlandish plant with blue nodules at the end of each branch that produce an eerie rattling sound from time to time.

Plant details: Tentacular aberrations are a wild plant that cannot be cultivated, and it needs minimum terrain fertility of 0.05. Can be harvested for tentacular fruit.

Based on artwork by Rob Smyth, https://robsmythart.com/projects

A sickly pink orb supported by a network of gnarled branches. A reddish sap constantly drips from its wood, and seems to keep insects at bay.

Plant details: Globular aberrations are a wild plant that cannot be cultivated, and it needs minimum terrain fertility of 0.05. Can be harvested for red wood.

Based on artwork by Rob Smyth, https://robsmythart.com/projects

A spiny plant with some kind of fruit hanging from its top. The fruit seems to be as hard as the trunk itself, and equally covered in spines.\n\nPlant details: Blood bouquet is a wild plant that cannot be cultivated, and it needs minimum terrain fertility of 0.05. Can be harvested for raw blood bouquet.

This ocular tree has been affected by pollution and mutated in strange ways. Concerningly, it seems to actually be flourishing in these conditions.\n\nPlant details: Mutated ocular trees are a wild plant, and they need minimum terrain fertility of 0.05. Can only grow in polluted terrains. Can be harvested for small amounts of Red Wood. Tree lover ideologies don't much care about chopping down these weird trees.

This globular aberration has been affected by pollution and mutated in strange ways. Concerningly, it seems to actually be flourishing in these conditions.\n\nPlant details: Polluted globular aberrations are a wild plant, and they need minimum terrain fertility of 0.05. Can only grow in polluted terrains. Can be harvested for small amounts of Red Wood. Tree lover ideologies don't much care about chopping down these weird trees.
A small anima-touched cactus. Hums faintly with psychic life. They can be harvested for wood.
An anima-touched cactus. Hums faintly with psychic life. They can be harvested for wood.
A large anima-touched cactus. Hums faintly with psychic life. They can be harvested for wood.

An anima-touched palm. It lacks the psychic potency of a true anima tree, but still hums faintly with psychic life.\n\nPlant details: Anima palms are wild plants that cannot be cultivated, and they need minimum terrain fertility of 0.05. They can be harvested for wood.
A small ocular cactus. Is it looking at you?\n\nPlant details: Ocular cacti are wild plants that cannot be cultivated, and they need minimum terrain fertility of 0.05. Can be harvested for red wood.

An ocular cactus. It is definitely keeping an eye (or several) on the colonists.

Plant details: Ocular cacti are wild plants that cannot be cultivated, and they need minimum terrain fertility of 0.05. Can be harvested for red wood.

Based on artwork by Ulysse Verhasselt, https://www.artstation.com/artwork/ORkP8

A spiny plant with some unusual fleshy tentacles sprouting from the top. Seems to be a variation of the blood bouquet found in ocular forests, but the fruit is inedible.\n\nPlant details: Desert bouquet is a wild plant that cannot be cultivated, and it needs minimum terrain fertility of 0.05.
A hardy, low-growing plant with distinctive lobed leaves that spreads into dense, verdant carpets across the forest floor.
A towering tree whose broad canopy is formed from oversized clover-shaped leaves, casting cool shade over the forest below. It doesn't yield much usable wood.
A peculiar tree with broad, flat leaves resembling giant lilypads, forming layered canopies above the forest floor.

An easy answer to the question: "what would you create if you were an insane plant geneticist?". This whimsical tree with a sugary trunk, frosting-like growths, and fruit that resembles glazed confections lures animals and colonists alike with the promise of edible delights.\n\nPlant details: Dessert trees are wild plants, and they need minimum terrain fertility of 0.7. Can be harvested for wood and fine desserts.
Wild grass modified to look like giant sugarcanes.

A weird combination of a tree, a mushroom, whipped cream, chocolate... sprinkles... Ok, very, very weird.\n\nPlant details: Chocolate trees are wild plants, and they need minimum terrain fertility of 0.7. Can be harvested for wood and chocolate.
Strange plants genetically modified to look like giant lollipops.

A grotesque growth of pulsing, veiny tissue stretched over a warped wooden frame. Its "bark" oozes with coagulated sap that smells faintly of blood.

Plant details: Flesh trees are wild plants, and they need minimum terrain fertility of 0.7. Can be harvested for wood and twisted flesh.

Inspired by art by Prajwal K Kumar https://www.artstation.com/prajwalkkumar

An irregular tumorous growth that swells from the ground like diseased flesh, spreading across the landscape.

Plant details: fleshy tumors are wild plants, and they need minimum terrain fertility of 0.7. Can be harvested for twisted flesh.

Inspired by No Man's Sky.

A fleshy tendril that erupts from the ground, twisting and writhing as though part of some unseen organism.\n\nPlant details: flesh tentacles are wild plants, and they need minimum terrain fertility of 0.7. Can be harvested for twisted flesh.
Orange tinted grass that moves silently in the wind.
Symbiotic moss that grows in Gauranlen groves.
A short orange-tinted shrub. Does not typically talk without alcohol being involved.
Tangled, thorny, woody shoots covered with orange leaves. Brambles grow in clusters, and slow down anyone moving over them.

An enormous relative of the Gauranlen tree. Though it shares the same distinctive appearance and faint psychic resonance, it no longer produces dryads. Some believe these giants are ancient Gauranlens whose inner queens have long since fallen dormant, while others claim they are the timeless homes of powerful nature spirits.
A short mauve shrub. Does not typically talk without alcohol being involved.
Tangled, thorny, woody shoots covered with mauve leaves. Brambles grow in clusters, and slow down anyone moving over them.
A graceful tree with dense mauve foliage that constantly exudes thick, syrupy droplets.\n\nBased on artwork by Splix04, https://splix04.itch.io
A bunch of poisonous looking flowers.
A bunch of dry terrain flowers.
A fern adapted to a dry climate.\n\nPlant details: Dry fern is a wild plant that cannot be cultivated.

A poisonous looking bush adapted to toxic environments.

Plant details: Toxic bush is a wild plant that cannot be cultivated.

Based on artwork by Splix04, https://splix04.itch.io

A cluster of large, trumpet-shaped blossoms reminiscent of morning glories. These giant flowers were genetically modified by a long-forgotten genetics company. These seem to be blooming almost continuously. Their stalks are not strong enough to be used as a wood substitute, but they are incredibly pretty.\n\nPlant details: Giant trumpetglory is a wild plant that cannot be cultivated. Very beautiful.

Giant flowers genetically modified by a long-forgotten genetics company using the genome of a rose. These seem to be blooming almost continuously. Their stalks are very strong and durable, so they can be cut and used as a wood substitute.\n\nPlant details: Giant pale rose is a wild plant that cannot be cultivated. Can be harvested for wood.

A continously blooming giant flower with a dangerous, bright pink colour. Its stalk can be cut and used as a wood substitute.\n\nPlant details: Giant toxic flowers are wild plants that cannot be cultivated. Can be harvested for meager amounts of wood.

A continously blooming giant flower. Its stalk can be cut and used as a wood substitute.\n\nPlant details: Giant toxic hornbloom are wild plants that cannot be cultivated. Can be harvested for meager amounts of wood.

These rare trees grow giant, shimmering golden cubes in place of fruit. Their trunks are smooth and warm, radiating a gentle comfort. When the wind rustles their leaves, the cubes chime softly, like distant laughter. Though they offer no practical boon beyond wood and gold, standing beneath one feels inexplicably reassuring.

Plant details: Golden cube trees are wild plants, and they need minimum terrain fertility of 0.7. Can be harvested for wood and gold.

Based on art by Sofia da Silva https://fisilva.artstation.com/projects/bkaDn

A bizarre fusion of bark and circuitry, this half-synthetic tree hums with low energy pulses. It grows like a plant, but responds like a machine. Small amounts of circuitry can be extracted from them, making industrial-grade components a renewable resource in this region.

Plant details: Techno trees are wild plants, and they need minimum terrain fertility of 0.7. Can be harvested for wood and components.

Inspired by art by Prajwal K Kumar https://www.artstation.com/prajwalkkumar

A tree-like giant bramble that supports a huge globe of glowing sap that casts a soft, colorful light in the dark. Its branches cradle the orb like a lantern, and the liquid inside gently swirls with bioluminescent energy.

Plant details: Luminescent trees are wild plants, and they need minimum terrain fertility of 0.7. Can be harvested for wood.

Inspired by art by Prajwal K Kumar https://www.artstation.com/prajwalkkumar
A graceful tree with long, sweeping branches draped in slender leaves that sway with the slightest breeze. It doesn't yield much usable wood.
A hardy tree with unique fan-shaped leaves, renowned for its resilience and spectacular golden foliage.

Half-alive, half-dead, this plant seems to be partly organic and partly inorganic. Its living tissues persist within a greenish shell of mineralized growth, slowly replacing stems, leaves, and roots with stone-like structures. Yet beneath the calcified exterior, faint signs of life remain.

Plant details: Calcified remnants are wild plants, and they need minimum terrain fertility of 0.7. Can be harvested for minute amounts of wood and random stone chunks.

Inspired by No Man's Sky.

This crystalline organism grows and pulses with faint signs of life, its mineral body constantly shifting and regenerating. They were originally created as a bioengineered solution to alcyonite mining, but inevitably spread into the wild.

Plant details: Living alcyonite are wild "plants", and they need minimum terrain fertility of 0.7. Can be harvested for alcyonite chunks.

Inspired by No Man's Sky.

A different archotech from the one transforming this region has initiated a hostile takeover, infusing the sessile mechanoids here with a mechanite virus that corrupts them into twisted creations.

Plant details: Mechanoid corruptions are wild plants, and they need minimum terrain fertility of 0.1. Can be harvested for minute amounts of wood.

Inspired by No Man's Sky.

A different archotech from the one transforming this region has initiated a hostile takeover, infusing the sessile mechanoids here with a mechanite virus that corrupts them into twisted creations.

Plant details: Corrupted mech nodes are wild plants, and they need minimum terrain fertility of 0.1. Can be harvested for minute amounts of wood.

Inspired by No Man's Sky.

These otherworldly plants grow within hollow marble lattices shaped like enormous teeth, using the casing for support and protection as their roots spread beneath the sands. A bizarre creation of an insane geneticist, their name and origins long lost to the centuries.\n\nPlant details: Giant false teeth are wild plants, and they need minimum terrain fertility of 0.1. Can be harvested for marble blocks and a bit of ancient bone.

This strange flower seems to be only partially organic. Part of its structure is clearly crystalline, and it appears to be unaffected, or even bolstered, by the extremely cold climate. It might even be edible.\n\nPlant details: Crystal horn is a wild plant that cannot be cultivated, and it needs minimum terrain fertility of 0.25. It grows in low temperatures (above -65ºC, below 10ºC) and needs no light. Can be harvested for raw crystal horn.

These translucent plants seem to be able to grow almost anywhere, even in some snow covered areas. They can be dried in a fire and used to feed herbivore animals efficiently. 

Plant details: Frost leaf is a wild plant that cannot be cultivated, and it needs minimum terrain fertility of 0. It grows in low temperatures (above -65ºC, below 10ºC) and needs no light. Can be harvested for raw frost leaf.

Inspired by art by Desiree-m. Deviantart page no longer exists :(

A very strange plant, partly inorganic, that seems to extract propane from the surrounding landscape and store it as an energy source in rime-bound chemical sacs. These sacs can be consumed as a very mild euphoric.\n\nPlant details: Rime nodules is a wild plant that cannot be cultivated, and it needs minimum terrain fertility of 0. It grows in low temperatures (above -65ºC, below 10ºC) and needs no light. Can be harvested for raw rime nodules.

A tall, translucent flower that seems to be partially inorganic.\n\nPlant details: Crystal flowers are a wild plant that cannot be cultivated, and it needs minimum terrain fertility of 0.25. It grows in low temperatures (above -65ºC, below 10ºC) and needs no light. Can be harvested for crystalline wood.

This tree, which probably started growing in a rare period of summer heat, has been frozen in place by the extreme temperatures, its leaves crystallized by the toxic propane compounds. A small amount of wood can be extracted from it, but it is likely that more of them won't appear as time passes.\n\nPlant details: Flash frozen trees appear in the wild but they don't regrow, ever. They need minimum terrain fertility of 0. Can be harvested for normal wood.

The brown barrel cactus, Ferocactus Brunetus, is an extremophile plant that thrives in low-water and poor sunlight conditions. Its strange brown colour is derived from an almost complete lack of chlorophyll. Instead, the plant extracts much of its sustenance from mineral deposits.

Plant details: brown barrel cactus is a wild plant that cannot be cultivated, and it needs minimum terrain fertility of 0.05. It needs no light. It is non-flammable. Can be harvested for raw brown barrel cactus, edible but almost tasteless.

Inspired by art by Desiree-m. Deviantart page no longer exists :(
Wild grass. Grows anywhere there is a little light and minimally fertile ground.

Firevine trees are pyrophitic plants that are able to survive wildfires due to a clever layer of thermal insulation provided by their fire retardant bark. They can be directly burned without sustaining damage to their vital tissues. In fact, their seeds require fire to sprout, so they are only found in fire-prone areas, such as active volcanic zones.\n\nPlant details: Firevine trees are a cultivated plant that also appear in the wild, and they need minimum terrain fertility of 0.05. They are non-flammable. Can be harvested for normal wood.
A wild tall fern. Slows down anyone moving over it.

This vivid green plant seem to be related to cacti. Though it's fleshy bark is not edible, it produces flowers than can be consumed by humans.\n\nPlant details: Iashiphus is a wild plant that cannot be cultivated, and it needs minimum terrain fertility of 0.7. Can be harvested for raw iashiphus fruit.

The sugar famewort grows in areas with a high concentration of pollinating insects. It generates a sweet nectar that attracts these insects, and they disperse its pollen when they feed on it.\n\nPlant details: Sugar Famewort is a wild plant that cannot be cultivated, and it needs minimum terrain fertility of 0.7. Can be harvested for raw sugar famewort.
Tangled, thorny, woody shoots covered with leaves. Raven nettle grows in clusters, and slows down anyone moving over it.

This exuberant palm grows in areas with a rich soil surrounding the tar pits.\n\nPlant details: Fan palms are a cultivated plant that also appear in the wild, and it needs minimum terrain fertility of 0.85. Can be harvested for normal wood.

The keening cordax is a carnivore plant so called for the high-pitched sound that it makes during the day. Its huge openings are filled with a smelly, sticky substance that attracts all kinds of small insects. These insects get stuck to this organic glue, and inevitably perish, serving as food for the plant.

This sticky substance, known as cordax resin, can be used as a very efficient sealant.

Plant details: Keening cordax is a wild plant that cannot be cultivated, and it needs minimum terrain fertility of 0.7. Can be harvested for cordax resin.
This is a puddle of fresh tar. No animal would eat this, right?
Steel pipes designed to transport pressurized liquid propane.
Subterranean steel pipes designed to transport pressurized liquid propane.

An industrial liquid storage tank meant for storing pressurized propane delivered via propane pipe network. Tanks can be designated to be siphoned for usable propane as needed. If damaged even lightly the escaping fumes will very swiftly create a gaseous fireball, the size of the resulting explosion will depend on the amount stored within.
A hopper-like storage basin meant to hold dispensed propane from storage tanks periodically for use later.
A hopper-like storage basin meant to input propane into the network, filling up connected storage tanks.
Extracts propane from a liquid propane lake and refines it into usable fuel.

A dryad caste specialized in general protection and utility. Companion dryads are strong, fierce and loyal. They can clean, haul, fight and carry packs in caravans.\n\nIn general, dryads are mammal-like creatures that have a symbiotic relationship with the Gauranlen tree. They reproduce together with their tree, which contains a hidden dryad queen. Dryads can morph into various specialized castes.
This small poison dart has been filled with the pungent resin flowing from a dribbling cap fungus. It is an extremely potent neurotoxin, causing immediate paralysis, and eventually, death.
A hard, pinkish looking mineral deposit.
A hard, pinkish looking mineral deposit. The layers have been polished to a flat, smooth surface.
A chunk of rock. It's possible to cut usable stone blocks from it.
A dark-hued, homogeneous metamorphic rock. These rocks seem to be attracting the darkness surrounding them.
A dark-hued, homogeneous metamorphic rock. These rocks seem to be attracting the darkness surrounding them.
A chunk of rock. It's possible to cut usable stone blocks from it.

Onyxglass is a rare volcanic glass formed when lava cools rapidly with trace impurities, giving it a deep luster and layered appearance. Like obsidian, it is hard, brittle, and amorphous, fracturing into exceptionally sharp edges.

My hands are shaking. It's as if the world has lost all colours.
Those rime nodules I consumed make me feel refreshed and calm.
I feel connected to something ancient.

The healing properties of the water rejuvenated me.
This place reeks of mold and decay, I can't stay outdoors for long!

Actually... I love this fog. This fog is my friend. I would kiss the fog if I could. Obey. Consume. Caress an ocular jelly. Wait, what?
Oh, this is actually pretty nice.
Something in this area makes all animals explode violently on death.
This area contains a wayward Agarilux Prime growing outside the Mycotic Jungle. It will release spores that destroy everything surrounding it.
This area has begun to transform into an ocular forest.
Weird flesh trees grow wild in this area. They don't look tasty.
Weird dessert trees grow wild in this area. They look VERY tasty.
A strange kind of trees grows in this area. They appear to be half synthetic.
Unusual luminescent trees grow in this area.
No wild plants grow here besides simple grass, but disease chance is lowered by 75%.
A shallow pool of a dense tar-like substance. Impassable, and can't be bridged over.
Lakes of liquid hydrocarbons that seem to defy the laws of physics.
